messages:
asha: quick q — sales says Acme wants a full weights export (quantized, 4-bit) for their on-prem appliance. They want a tarball we can hand off and permission to use commercially/resell. is this something we can approve? :thinking:
leah (legal): short answer: probably not under our standard upstream license. we need to check the model's original license and any downstream restrictions. quantized copies usually still count as 'derivatives' in most licenses i know.
riley: to add a technical angle — our quant pipeline would produce a packaged artifact (model.bin + config + vocab). from a legal POV is that "distribution" or is it "providing a hosted service"?
leah (legal): handing over the packaged artifact is distribution. hosting a model behind our API is not. so giving them a tarball = redistribution.
mina: customer argues they need it for air-gapped use and compliance. business would prefer to sign a commercial addendum rather than say no. are we set up to do bespoke licensing?
leah (legal): we can do a bespoke commercial license, but need signoff from upstream rights holders if the original license forbids commercial redistribution. options: 1) ask upstream for a commercial sublicense 2) deny export and offer Dedicated/Private deployment with data-processor terms 3) build a transfer-of-custody agreement with strict usage audits.
tom-ops: operationally, shipping a quantized copy also means we may be shipping optimized kernels or conversion scripts. those could include our proprietary tooling — that'll complicate things. we should strip any internal binaries and only ship the bare quant weights + minimal loader if we go that route.
riley: question — if we only provide float32 weights and let them run their own quantization, does that change the license interpretation?
leah (legal): not really — original weights in any format are still the original work. quantizing on their side vs ours doesn't avoid redistribution concerns.
asha: sales pushed back: "we need a yes/no today". what's the pragmatic short path?
mina: pragmatic path = offer Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem package) with a time-limited trial, and a cost uplift for on-prem maintenance. that meets customer needs without redistributing weights.
leah (legal): agree. escalate to upstream only if customer insists on transfer. meanwhile, propose the commercial addendum template to engineering and product to estimate effort.
riley: if we do need to explore an export path, can eng prepare a sanitized export: remove internal optimizations, provide a standard loader, document fingerprinting (so we can trace copies)?
tom-ops: yes we can produce a minimal artifact, and we can embed a watermark hash in the metadata. but legal needs to confirm if embedding fingerprinting is allowed by the upstream license.
policy-bot: <policy doc> https://intranet.redwood.ai/policies/model-exports — contains checklist: upstream-license, commercial-sublicense, toolchain-audit, artifact-sanitization.
leah (legal): next steps: (1) sales to get explicit upstream model id + license text from provider; (2) eng to estimate sanitization effort and confirm whether any proprietary bits would leak; (3) legal to draft conditional commercial addendum. i'll loop in counsel if upstream says no.
asha: thanks — i'll ping sales and loop back with model artifact + license. :white_check_mark:
